claims.text: An abstract data type (ADT) is a collection of data together with a set of operations on those data, described by what the operations do rather than how they are stored.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The stack, the queue and the linked list are examples of ADTs: each is data plus its named operations, and the operations are what the user of the ADT sees.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A stack is a last-in-first-out structure: push adds an item to the top and pop removes the most recently pushed item, so the newest item leaves first.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A queue is a first-in-first-out structure: enqueue adds an item at the rear and dequeue removes the item at the front, so the oldest item leaves first.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A linked list is a chain of nodes, each holding a data value and a pointer to the next node, so items are reached by following the chain from the start.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Adding, editing and deleting in these structures uses the structure's own operations and their order rules: a stack is changed at the top, a queue at both ends, a linked list by redirecting pointers.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: In an array implementation, each node of a linked list is a pair of array elements - the data value and a pointer holding the index of the next node - and at AS a pointer is an index into an array.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A stack is implemented with an array and a pointer named Top holding the index of the top element; a queue with an array and pointers named Front and Rear holding the indices of the queue's two ends.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: An implementation names the arrays, their data types, the pointer variables and their initial values - behaviour alone is not an implementation, because an implementation declares things.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).
